exercise.name: Single-Arm Cable Hammer Curl
library_steps: Stand side-on to a low pulley holding a rope or handle, palm facing in.
Curl it up to your shoulder with your thumb on top.
Lower slowly, finish your reps, then switch arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing side-on to a low pulley, a D-handle in one hand with the palm facing in (thumb on top); the upper arm stays by the side while the elbow bends from ~13 to ~124 deg. Biceps and brachioradialis share the work; the other hand rests on the hip.

setup.target: Low pulley beside the working foot (side-on).
Neutral: palm facing the body, thumb up.
setup.why: Library step; neutral grip raises the brachioradialis share (S1).

movement.measure: upper arm from the torso side line

muscles.emg: Main elbow flexor in curls (EMG and hypertrophy, see sources).
muscles.role: Bends the elbow; what the exercise is for.

muscles.emg: Brachioradialis clearly active in curls; its share rises with the hand turned toward neutral/pronated (S on hand position).
muscles.role: Helps bend the elbow; library secondary.
muscles.surface: Thumb side of the upper forearm.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The hand rolls into a normal curl.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The hammer grip is the point (thumb on top).

sources.citation: Kleiber T, Kunz L, Disselhorst-Klug C. 2015. Muscular coordination of biceps brachii and brachioradialis in elbow flexion with respect to hand position. Front Physiol 6:215.
sources.what_it_gave: Elbow flexion with the hand pronated, neutral and supinated: brachioradialis share rises significantly with the hand pronated (palms down); biceps activity unchanged.

sources.citation: Larsen S, Sandvik Kristiansen B, Osteras Sandberg N, et al. 2026. The effects of shoulder extension angle on elbow flexor hypertrophy in the cable curl exercise. Front Physiol 17:1750722.
sources.what_it_gave: Unilateral cable curls from a low pulley with the upper arm by the side (neutral) vs held back in shoulder extension: elbow flexors grew ~7-9 % in both; the shoulder angle made no clear difference.
